subject: business-studies
title: Cash Flow Forecasts
welcome_lead: Cash, not profit, pays the bills - forecast it carefully.
meta_desc: A-Level Finance: cash flow forecast structure, opening and closing balances.
final_note: Profitable businesses still fail when cash runs out - forecasting is survival.

concepts.def: Cash paid out during the period.
Inflows minus outflows for the period.

Opening balance plus net cash flow.
Inability to pay debts when due - cash crisis.

walkthroughs.body_html: List monthly inflows (sales receipts, loans) and outflows (rent, wages, supplies). Net them, add to opening balance - you get the closing balance, which becomes next month's opening.
Profit can be earned on credit and not yet received as cash. A firm growing fast often suffers from overtrading: profitable orders but no cash to pay wages.

Options include chasing debtors faster, negotiating longer supplier credit, leasing rather than buying assets, or arranging an overdraft. Each has a cost - interest, lost discounts or strained relationships.

mcqs.q: A profitable firm can still fail because of:
options: Strong sales growth
Poor cash flow management
Low capital employed
Falling gearing

mcqs.q: Why can a profitable business still fail?
options: Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
If a business is profitable it cannot run out of money.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
Because cash flow and profit are different — a business may be profitable on paper but run out of cash to pay bills, especially if customers owe money or stock ties up funds.

mcqs.q: Why are cash flow and profit different on different time-scales?
options: Cash flow only matters at year-end.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Cash flow and profit are the same thing measured differently.

Profit is recognised when a sale is made (even on credit); cash flow is when money actually moves. A profitable sale today may produce no cash for 60 days while bills are due — creating a cash-flow problem despite profit.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?
options: Gross profit = revenue minus cost of goods sold (direct costs only); net profit = revenue minus ALL costs including overheads, interest and tax. Net profit is the bottom line.
Gross profit and net profit are the same thing.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Cash flow only matters at year-end.
